title: Claude Fable 5 & Mythos 5
content:
## Overview

On June 9, 2026, Anthropic released **Claude Fable 5** and **Claude Mythos 5** — the first models in a new "Mythos-class" tier that sits above the Opus tier. Fable 5 is the publicly available variant; Mythos 5 is the same underlying model with certain safety classifiers removed, available only to vetted cyber-defense and infrastructure providers through Anthropic's **Project Glasswing** program.

---

## The Mythos-Class Tier

Anthropic introduced Mythos-class to acknowledge that the capability gap between this generation and Opus is large enough to warrant a new naming tier — the first change to the Haiku / Sonnet / Opus structure since it debuted with Claude 3. Two variants ship the same weights under different safety postures:

- **Fable 5 (general availability):** Full safety classifiers enabled. When a request touches flagged domains — cybersecurity exploits, dual-use biology, and similar — the model automatically falls back to Claude Opus 4.8. Anthropic reports this fallback triggers in fewer than 5% of sessions, meaning more than 95% of requests run directly on the Mythos-class weights.
- **Mythos 5 (restricted access):** The same model without the safety fallback, available only through Project Glasswing to organizations vetted for offensive security research, critical infrastructure defense, and related use cases.

---

## Key Specifications

| Feature | Value |
|---|---|
| Context window | 1,000,000 tokens |
| Max output tokens | 128,000 |
| Thinking mode | Always-on adaptive thinking |
| General availability date | June 9, 2026 |
| Pricing (input / output) | $10 / $50 per million tokens |
| API model ID | `claude-fable-5` |

Pricing is double Claude Opus 4.8 on both dimensions ($5/$25 per million). Anthropic's position is that token efficiency on complex tasks makes the effective cost competitive.

---

## Benchmark Performance

### Software Engineering

| Benchmark | Fable 5 / Mythos 5 | Opus 4.8 | GPT-5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SWE-Bench Pro | **80.3%** | 69.2% | 58.6% | 54.2% |
| FrontierCode (Cognition) | **29.3%** | 13.4% | 5.7% | — |

FrontierCode evaluates demanding coding tasks under production standards (correctness, test coverage, style). The gap between Fable 5 and the next model is wider here than on SWE-Bench, suggesting a qualitative difference in how the model handles realistic engineering constraints.

### Knowledge Work & Reasoning

| Benchmark | Fable 5 / Mythos 5 | Opus 4.8 | GPT-5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GDPval-AA | **1,932** | 1,890 | 1,769 | 1,314 |
| Humanity's Last Exam (no tools) | **59.0%** | 49.8% | 41.4% | 44.4% |
| Humanity's Last Exam (with tools) | **64.5%** | 57.9% | 52.2% | 51.4% |

### Cybersecurity

Claude Mythos 5 scores **78.0%** on cybersecurity evaluations — nearly double Opus 4.8's 40.0%. This gap is the primary reason Mythos 5 is restricted to vetted access; Anthropic judged that the uplift it provides in offensive domains required additional safeguards.

---

## Token Efficiency in Practice

One early customer reported that Fable 5 completed a frontier physics research task in **36 hours** using **one-third the reasoning tokens** that GPT-5.5 required over four days. At Fable 5's $10/M input price vs. GPT-5.5's $5/M, using 3× fewer tokens makes the effective cost lower despite the higher per-token rate. This matches Anthropic's claim that adaptive thinking mode reduces wasted computation on simpler sub-tasks within a session.

---

## Export Control Suspension (June 12, 2026)

Three days after launch, Anthropic announced it had received a US government export-control directive requiring suspension of access to both Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 for certain jurisdictions. Anthropic did not disclose the specific jurisdictions or the expected duration. Claude Opus 4.8 remained unaffected and continued as the flagship generally available model for affected users.
